references.text: First description of the manna in the wilderness, where it is described as something fine and granular that lay on the ground.
The manna is described here as white and like coriander seed, with a taste like honey cakes. Provides further details about the appearance of the manna.
Bedolach (bdellium) is mentioned here in connection with the land of Havilah, the same material that the appearance of the manna is compared to.
Moses reminds the people how God gave them manna in the wilderness, food that neither they nor their fathers had known.
Another reference to manna as food in the wilderness, which their fathers did not know.
The psalm describes how God let manna rain down from heaven and gave the people bread from heaven to eat.
Jesus refers to the manna that the fathers ate in the wilderness, the bread from heaven.
Jesus mentions again the manna that the fathers ate in the wilderness.
The hidden manna is mentioned as a promise to the one who overcomes, a typological connection to the manna in the wilderness.
